tagline: A Basque industrial port reborn as an art city, Bilbao is home to Frank Gehry's titanium Guggenheim Museum, a medieval Old Town and some of Spain's best pintxos.
overview: Bilbao, the largest city in the Basque Country, was a centre of iron, steel and shipbuilding until heavy industry declined in the late 20th century. The city reinvented itself, and the opening of Frank Gehry's Guggenheim Museum in 1997 transformed its image, an effect now known as the 'Bilbao effect'.

The museum's curving titanium walls sit on the Nervión River, guarded by Jeff Koons' flower-covered Puppy and Louise Bourgeois' giant spider, Maman. Riverside walkways link it to the Fine Arts Museum, Calatrava's Zubizuri bridge and the old docks.

Across the river, the Casco Viejo's Seven Streets are packed with pintxos bars around the Plaza Nueva. The Artxanda funicular climbs to city views, and the UNESCO-listed Vizcaya Bridge, the world's oldest transporter bridge, swings cars and people across the river mouth.

funFacts.title: SEVEN STREETS
